newsitem.title: CHINA: China unveils plant, animal quarantine rules.
newsitem.headline: China unveils plant, animal quarantine rules.

text.p: China on Sunday announced detailed regulations for the quarantine of plants and animals brought in and out of the country, and placed management of inspections under a single state quarantine bureau.
Under the regulations, which will take effect on January 1, 1997, the bureau will collect information on plant and animal epidemics both domestically and abroad, the official Xinhua news agency said.
Xinhua said plants or seeds brought into the country will require seven-day prior notification while prior notification for animals will range from 15 to 30 days.
The regulations also state the authority of inspectors to board ships, planes, trains or vehicles on entry into the country and the procedures for handling contaminated or diseased plants or animals.
The regulations also state the legal reponsibilities of individuals or companies bringing in banned or restricted plants or animals.
